# Sherlock WAF control-plane API reference

<!-- Generated by `make gen` from api/openapi.yaml. Do not edit. -->

Version 1.0.0. Every path below is relative to `/api/v1`.

The one public API: the dashboard, the CLI and automation all use `/api/v1`.
Conventions are in docs/architecture/api.md. Errors are RFC 9457 problem
documents. Config objects carry an `ETag` (the config version id); writes need
`If-Match` (missing: 428, stale: 412).

Every operation declares `x-sherlock-permission`, the only input to
authorisation: `public`, `authenticated`, or a named permission. A route with
no permission is refused at start-up and in CI.

Authentication is a dashboard session cookie (non-GET requests also need the `X-CSRF-Token` header) or an API token sent as `Authorization: Bearer shk_<id>_<secret>`. The permission column names what the caller needs; `public` needs none. The full schemas are in [api/openapi.yaml](../../api/openapi.yaml).

### `GET /system/update`

Check whether a newer signed release is available

Fetches the signed release manifest through the SSRF-safe client, verifies its signature
with the release key built into the binary and compares versions. Results are cached for
five minutes. A failed check is a 502, never a stale "up to date".

Operation `getUpdateStatus`. Permission: `system:read`.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 501 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 502 | An RFC 9457 problem document |

### `POST /system/update/apply`

Download, verify and stage or install the latest signed release

Verifies the manifest signature and archive checksum, refuses downgrades, then either replaces
the binary (when the process may write it) or stages the verified bundle in the data directory,
where the service unit installs it, after verifying it again as root, at the next start.
Never restarts the process: the response says what to do. Audited as `system.update`. Refused
inside containers, where the image is updated instead.

Operation `applyUpdate`. Permission: `system:update`.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Staged or installed |
| 403 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 409 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 422 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 501 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 502 | An RFC 9457 problem document |

### `POST /system/upstream/test`

Check that the proxy can reach an upstream target (connect and HEAD /, no redirects, 3 s)

Operation `testUpstream`. Permission: `config:write`.

Request body (`application/json`, required): `TestUpstreamRequest`

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Result (a failed check is still 200 with reachable=false) |
| 400 | An RFC 9457 problem document |

## setup

### `POST /setup/admin`

Create the first administrator (only while no user exists; needs the one-time setup token)

The setup token is printed to the server's log at start-up while the node has no users.
It is compared in constant time, single-use per process lifetime, and the endpoint closes
itself as soon as any user exists. Attempts are throttled.

Operation `createFirstAdmin`. Permission: `public`.

Request body (`application/json`, required): `FirstAdminRequest`

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 201 | Created |
| 400 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 403 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 409 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 429 | An RFC 9457 problem document |

### `GET /setup/status`

Whether first-run setup is still open (no users exist)

Operation `getSetupStatus`. Permission: `public`.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |

### `POST /sites/{site}/exclusions`

Add an exclusion; the change is audited with the actor and, when created from an event, the event id

Rejects with 422 when the exclusion has critical warnings (for example a
whole attack category) unless `acknowledge_warnings` is true.

Operation `createExclusion`. Permission: `config:write`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `site` | path | string | yes |  |
| `If-Match` | header | string | no | ETag of the version you read. Required to change an existing configuration (428 if missing, 412 if stale). |

Request body (`application/json`, required): `ExclusionCreate`

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 201 | The version now live |
| 404 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 409 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 412 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 422 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 428 | An RFC 9457 problem document |

### `POST /sites/{site}/exclusions/propose`

Propose the narrowest exclusion for an event, or preview one you edited, with past-event impact and warnings

With `event_id` the server builds the narrowest exclusion (this rule,
this target, this path, this method). With `exclusion` it only evaluates
the given one (use it when the user widens the proposal in the wizard).
Nothing is saved.

Operation `proposeExclusion`. Permission: `events:read`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `site` | path | string | yes |  |

Request body (`application/json`, required): `ExclusionProposalRequest`

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 400 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 404 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 422 | An RFC 9457 problem document |

### `GET /sites/{site}/paranoia-impact`

Predicted additional blocks if the blocking paranoia level is raised, from stored findings

Needs findings recorded above the current blocking level, i.e. the site's
`paranoia_level` (detection) must be at least `target`. When it is not,
`observable` is false and nothing can be predicted.

Operation `getParanoiaImpact`. Permission: `events:read`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `site` | path | string | yes |  |
| `target` | query | integer | yes |  |
| `from` | query | string (date-time) | no | Default 7 days before `to` |
| `to` | query | string (date-time) | no | Default now |

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 400 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
| 404 | An RFC 9457 problem document |
